title: Ensemble calibration cross-validation and confidence heuristics for JSON function-call resilience in low-precision inference
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: We observe intermittent JSON schema parse failures and subtle field corruption after switching serving profiles to aggressive FP8/INT8 runtime kernels. Single-run calibration results are noisy across prompt families. Goal: build an ensemble-based calibration cross-validation workflow and a lightweight runtime confidence heuristic that detects likely structured-output corruption (function-call JSON) and triggers automated fallback or re-calibration. Deliverables: (1) cross-validation harness that runs N calibration variants and aggregates per-field metrics; (2) runtime confidence score computed from token-level distribution + structural checks; (3) automated rollback/fallback policy and a validation dashboard for per-release quality gates.
acceptance_criteria: Ensemble cross-val harness produces stable per-field pass-rate with <2% variance across 10 seeds for golden prompt corpus
Runtime confidence score has precision >= 0.95 at 0.9 recall for detecting schema-violating outputs on validation set
CI gate prevents low-precision rollout if ensemble-validated structured-output fidelity drops >1.5% absolute vs baseline
End-to-end test (hosted runtime) demonstrates automated fallback to higher-precision variant under confidence threshold with <200ms additional latency for failure cases
approach: Construct a diverse golden prompt corpus covering edge-cases (nested objects, optional fields, varied ordering, escaped strings)
Run ensemble of calibration strategies: per-layer vs per-channel, symmetric vs asymmetric clipping, 8-bit integer range choices, FP8 exponent bias variants
Cross-validate by holding out prompt families and computing per-field exact-match, JSON-parse success, and parse-F1
Aggregate ensemble signals using voting + weighted confidence derived from token logits and field-level parse robustness
Instrument runtime to compute confidence score (token entropy + structural checksum + prefix-stability) and expose metric for rollout policies
experiments: Experiment A: 10-fold cross-validation across 12 prompt families, compare single-calib baseline vs ensemble median profile
Experiment B: Evaluate confidence heuristic thresholds on held-out 5k prompts with simulated traffic distribution
Experiment C: Canary rollout in dedicated pool with automatic fallback to INT8-safe model variant on low confidence
Experiment D: Ablation of structural checks (remove checksum or remove token-entropy term) to measure contribution
results_summary: Preliminary run (02/25): ensemble median reduced schema-parse failures from 3.8% -> 1.1% on golden corpus (N=1,000)
Confidence heuristic tuned to threshold 0.75 produced 94% precision / 88% recall on held-out set; plan to push recall to >=90% by adding prefix-stability term
Canary (03/01): 48-hour run in dedicated pool triggered fallback on 17 incidents; average additional latency for fallback path 140ms; no customer-facing errors observed
Ablation: removing token-entropy term increased false negatives by ~30% indicating token distribution important for detection
